headline: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
angle: An AI safety company devoted to alignment and efficiency realizes it's become a bloated corporate bureaucracy.
scene: A Slack message from a senior Anthropic engineer to their team: 'Can't ship the alignment fix today—I'm in back-to-back meetings about alignment.' Behind them, a calendar showing 8 consecutive 1-hour blocks. On their monitor, an unfinished code commit from 2 hours ago.
setup: Senior engineer to junior dev: 'We need to talk about why we're shipping slower.'
punchline: Their calendar loads for 30 seconds before responding.
instagram_caption: The irony of a company built to prevent AI from getting worse is that it's now just like every other company.
image_prompt: Single-panel cartoon, clean line art, thick black outlines, muted blue-gray pastel colors, white background, New Yorker magazine aesthetic, flat colors, no shading, no gradients, no signature. An engineer slouched in an office chair, staring exhaustedly at a computer screen showing a calendar full of meeting blocks in different colors. A second engineer standing nearby, gesturing. Papers and coffee cups on the desk. A large clock on the wall in the background showing 4:47 PM. The overall feeling is one of despair and resignation.
